package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via phishing and exploits, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: SmokeLoader is a modular malware loader that delivers and executes a variety of malicious plugins designed to steal credentials, exfiltrate sensitive data, inject code into legitimate processes, and maintain persistence on infected Windows systems. It leverages phishing, exploits, and multi-stage loaders to evade detection and maximize impact, using advanced techniques such as steganography, process injection, and API hooking to achieve its objectives.

execution_context.file_location: malicious Microsoft Office document (CVE-2017-0199 or CVE-2017-11882)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: OLE2-embedded link object or equation editor shellcode that downloads and executes a remote VBS file using URLDownloadToFile.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document-open, the embedded exploit executes shellcode that downloads a remote VBS file using URLDownloadToFile, writes it to disk, and executes it, initiating the malware infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of embedded shellcode in Office documents to download and execute remote scripts is a clear sign of exploitation and malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents do not contain hidden shellcode or objects that trigger code execution and download external scripts upon opening.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document templates may fetch data, but do not execute arbitrary code or download and run scripts from the internet.
key_indicators: Exploitation of CVE-2017-0199 or CVE-2017-11882 in Office documents
Automatic download and execution of remote VBS files via shellcode
Presence of OLE2-embedded objects with suspicious links

execution_context.file_location: HTA file or VBS file (downloaded by exploit)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated VBS script that decodes and executes PowerShell code to download another VBS file (AndeLoader).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At script execution, the obfuscated VBS decodes embedded PowerShell, which downloads the next-stage VBS loader (AndeLoader) from a remote server, writes it to disk, and executes it, continuing the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated scripts that decode and execute PowerShell to download further payloads are a hallmark of malware loaders and are rarely seen in legitimate automation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate VBS/HTA files do not typically contain multi-layered obfuscation or staged payload delivery mechanisms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise scripts may use PowerShell for automation, but not for multi-stage payload delivery or obfuscation.
key_indicators: Multiple layers of encoding/obfuscation in VBS/HTA files
PowerShell used to download and execute additional scripts

execution_context.file_location: AndeLoader VBS file (downloaded by previous stage)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Deobfuscated PowerShell code that downloads a steganographic image, extracts base64-encoded injector, decodes it, and executes dnlib.IO.Home.VAI method with arguments including the SmokeLoader payload URL.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the loader downloads a steganographic image from a remote server, extracts and decodes an embedded injector from the image, and executes the dnlib.IO.Home.VAI method with parameters to fetch and inject the SmokeLoader payload, enabling the next stage of infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of steganography to conceal payloads and dynamic code execution with attacker-controlled arguments is a strong indicator of sophisticated malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not use steganography to hide and execute code or dynamically load executables from images.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Steganography is rarely, if ever, used in legitimate enterprise automation or software deployment.
key_indicators: Steganographic payload delivery via image files
Dynamic extraction and execution of code from images
Use of dnlib.IO.Home.VAI method for code injection

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Class.Start method: Combines VBS files, writes persistence to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, downloads and injects SmokeLoader into RegAsm.exe by creating a suspended process, writing payload to memory, and modifying thread context to point to SmokeLoader entry point.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injector binary establishes persistence by modifying the registry Run key, downloads the SmokeLoader payload from a remote server, creates a suspended RegAsm.exe process, injects the payload into its memory, and modifies the thread context to execute SmokeLoader within the legitimate process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Registry persistence and process injection into system processes are classic malware techniques for stealth, persistence, and evasion.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not inject code into system processes or modify registry autorun keys to launch malicious scripts without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters use registry autorun for persistence, but do not perform process injection or code hollowing.
key_indicators: Creation of suspended processes and memory manipulation

execution_context.file_location: Injected into RegAsm.exe (or explorer.exe for plugins)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SmokeLoader main module: Connects to C2 server, downloads plugin configurations and encrypted plugin payloads, injects plugins into explorer.exe or other target processes using process hollowing and shellcode.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the SmokeLoader main module, running inside RegAsm.exe, establishes a connection to its C2 server, downloads encrypted plugin configurations and payloads, and injects these plugins into explorer.exe or other target processes using process hollowing and shellcode execution, enabling further malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: C2 communication, plugin-based architecture, and process injection into legitimate processes are advanced malware behaviors designed for stealth and modularity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not inject arbitrary code into system processes or download and execute untrusted plugins from remote servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate software uses this combination of C2-driven plugin delivery and process injection.
key_indicators: C2 communication for plugin delivery and configuration
Process injection into explorer.exe or other system processes
Encrypted payload delivery and dynamic code execution

execution_context.file_location: Injected into browsers, email clients, FTP clients, explorer.exe

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Plugins (1-9): API hooking code that intercepts credential storage/access APIs (e.g., vaultcli.dll, registry, SQLite files, wininet.dll, ws2_32.dll, user32.dll), extracts credentials, cookies, autofill data, clipboard content, and exfiltrates to C2.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, injected plugins hook sensitive APIs in target processes such as browsers, email clients, and FTP clients, intercept credential and data access, extract credentials, cookies, autofill data, and clipboard content, and exfiltrate this information to the attacker's C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: API hooking for credential theft and data exfiltration is a hallmark of advanced infostealers and is not found in legitimate plugins.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate plugins or extensions do not hook system APIs to steal and exfiltrate user data or credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security software may hook APIs for monitoring, but never for exfiltration of sensitive data.
key_indicators: API hooking in browsers, email clients, and FTP clients
Extraction of credentials, cookies, and clipboard data
Exfiltration of sensitive data to remote C2 servers

attack_chain.action: Victim receives phishing email with malicious Office document exploiting CVE-2017-0199 or CVE-2017-11882.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial code execution and download of VBS loader

attack_chain.action: Malicious VBS/HTA script executes, decodes PowerShell, and downloads AndeLoader.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of AndeLoader and download of steganographic payload

attack_chain.action: AndeLoader downloads steganographic image, extracts and decodes injector, and executes it with parameters for SmokeLoader.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of injector and download of SmokeLoader

attack_chain.action: Injector establishes persistence, downloads SmokeLoader, and injects it into RegAsm.exe.
SmokeLoader connects to C2, downloads plugin configurations and payloads, and injects plugins into explorer.exe or other targets.
Plugins hook APIs in browsers, email clients, FTP clients, and explorer.exe to steal credentials, cookies, clipboard data, and exfiltrate to C2.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration and completion of attack objectives

behavioral_signatures: Office document execution triggers download and execution of remote scripts exploiting CVE-2017-0199 or CVE-2017-11882
Obfuscated VBS/HTA scripts decoding and running PowerShell to download further payloads
Steganographic payload delivery and extraction of executables from image files
Registry Run key modification for persistence with suspicious VBS or binary paths
Process injection and hollowing into RegAsm.exe or explorer.exe
API hooking in browsers, email clients, and FTP clients for credential and data theft
Network communication with known C2 IPs/domains for payload and data exfiltration
file_indicators: Office documents exploiting CVE-2017-0199 or CVE-2017-11882
Obfuscated VBS/HTA files in user temp or downloads directories
Registry key: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run with suspicious VBS or binary path
Injected or hollowed RegAsm.exe or explorer.exe processes in memory
Downloaded steganographic image files used for payload extraction
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled servers for payload and plugin delivery
Exfiltration of credentials and sensitive data to remote C2 endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents that exploit CVE-2017-0199 or CVE-2017-11882 and trigger downloads or execution of scripts. Detect obfuscated VBS/HTA/PowerShell activity, especially multi-stage downloads and steganographic payload extraction from image files. Alert on registry Run key modifications pointing to suspicious scripts or binaries. Monitor for process injection or hollowing into RegAsm.exe or explorer.exe, and for API hooking in browsers and email clients. Correlate with known C2 IPs and domains, and flag unusual outbound traffic patterns consistent with payload delivery or data exfiltration.
